sections.name: Unit I - Introduction to Cloud Computing

questions.q: Which statement best defines cloud computing?
options: Use of remote servers over a network to provision computing resources on demand
Installation of software only on personal desktops
Manual scheduling of batch jobs on a single machine
Use of physical storage without any network access

questions.q: The term 'on-demand self-service' in cloud computing means that a user can:
options: Wait for a vendor technician to configure every server
Provision resources automatically without human intervention from the provider
Set up hardware physically in a data center on request
Install only licensed software from a local CD

questions.q: Elasticity in cloud computing is best described as the system's ability to:
options: Add or remove resources automatically to match demand
Use only one large server for all workloads
Store data in a fixed archive format

questions.q: Scalability is primarily concerned with:
options: The automatic increase or decrease of resources during runtime
The ability of a system to handle growth in workload or size
The backup strategy used after a disaster

questions.q: Which cloud characteristic means multiple customers share the same physical infrastructure while remaining logically isolated?
Resource pooling in cloud means:
options: Resources are kept idle until a customer manually requests them
A provider allocates a shared pool of resources across multiple users based on demand
All customers receive dedicated hardware in every case
Resources are always stored only in one geographical region

questions.q: Broad network access in the cloud requires that resources are:
options: Only accessible from a single workstation
Accessible via standard network mechanisms from multiple client platforms
Stored in a local private network only

questions.q: Measured service refers to cloud services being:
options: Available only for one customer at a time
Monitored, controlled, and billed according to actual usage
Configured only by provider staff through in-person visits
Restricted to a fixed monthly quota regardless of demand

questions.q: The pay-as-you-go model is most closely associated with:
Which concept is most closely related to cloud computing's treatment of hardware as a shared, abstracted resource?
Which of the following is a major advantage of cloud computing?
options: Complete elimination of all operational risk
Faster deployment and reduced upfront capital investment

questions.q: Which of the following is a common limitation or challenge in cloud adoption?
options: Security, privacy, and vendor lock-in concerns
Automatic zero downtime for every application

questions.q: Which of the following is the best comparison between traditional computing and cloud computing?
options: Traditional computing always requires only a browser-based interface, while cloud requires no infrastructure
Traditional computing usually relies on fixed local resources, while cloud offers scalable shared resources over a network
Traditional computing eliminates the need for virtualization, while cloud does not use it
Traditional computing is always public, while cloud is always private

questions.q: A company chooses cloud computing mainly because it wants to reduce capital expenditure and increase deployment speed. This is an example of:
Which statement correctly distinguishes distributed computing from parallel computing?
options: Distributed computing is always single-threaded, while parallel computing uses a central server only
Parallel computing often executes multiple tasks simultaneously on interconnected resources, while distributed computing emphasizes autonomous nodes connected by a network
Distributed computing cannot involve communication between nodes, while parallel computing always does
Parallel computing is only about storage, while distributed computing is only about processors

questions.q: Grid computing is best described as:
options: A single virtual machine running on a host
A network of loosely coupled computing resources shared across administrative domains
A database-only system for object storage

questions.q: Cluster computing differs from grid computing primarily because a cluster usually:
options: Spans independent organizations and is loosely coupled
Uses a tightly managed set of connected machines with common administration
Is only a software concept with no hardware
Supports only one application at a time

questions.q: Which of the following is the best example of edge computing?
options: Processing sensor data locally near the device instead of sending everything to a central cloud
Running a single database on a personal laptop
Uploading all files to a remote archive without filtering
Creating a local printer queue only

questions.q: Fog computing is best described as:
options: A cloud-only model with no local devices
Distributed computing between edge devices and centralized cloud, with intermediate local processing
The use of one VM per user with no sharing

questions.q: Serverless computing is different from traditional hosting because the user typically pays for:
options: The amount of actual code execution time or event-triggered work performed

questions.q: Cloud-native computing is most associated with:
options: Monolithic applications deployed entirely on one server
Designing systems for containerization, microservices, automation, and dynamic orchestration
Storing all data in a single text file on a desktop

questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding scalability and elasticity?
options: Scalability is always automatic, while elasticity is a static design property
Elasticity is about dynamic adjustment to workload, while scalability is about the system's ability to grow or shrink in capacity
Scalability is a network protocol, while elasticity is a storage feature
They are identical and can be used interchangeably in all contexts

questions.q: Availability and reliability are related but not identical because availability is about:
options: How long a system is functioning and accessible when needed
The number of storage snapshots retained
The cost of a cloud subscription

questions.q: Fault tolerance in a cloud system means the system can:
options: Ignore all failures and continue without monitoring
Continue operating correctly even when some components fail
Stop scaling permanently after a failure
Only recover from failures through manual reboot

questions.q: Agility in cloud adoption most directly refers to:
options: The ability to quickly create, deploy, and change resources in response to business needs
The cost per unit of bandwidth
The speed of a single CPU core
The number of physical disks in a rack

questions.q: Resource utilization in a shared cloud environment is improved when:
options: Servers are left idle and isolated for each workload
Resources are multiplexed efficiently among multiple consumers based on demand
Every customer gets a dedicated room-sized data center
No automation is used for scheduling

sections.name: Unit II - SOA, Virtualization, and Service-Oriented Computing

questions.q: Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) is primarily designed to support:
options: Loose coupling and reusable services over a network
Operating only on a single OS instance

questions.q: A service provider in SOA is best described as the entity that:
options: Consumes a service without implementing it
Provides a service or functionality to other components or users
Only stores logs in a local file

questions.q: In a service registry, the primary purpose is to:
options: Store service metadata so consumers can discover providers

questions.q: Loose coupling in SOA is beneficial because it:
options: Requires all systems to use the same programming language only
Reduces dependency between services and allows independent evolution

questions.q: Reusability in SOA allows a business capability to be:
options: Used only once in a single program
Composed into multiple applications without rewriting the logic

questions.q: Interoperability is most important when services need to:
options: Operate only on one vendor's platform
Communicate across different systems, technologies, or platforms
Be physically on the same machine without networking

questions.q: Composability in SOA refers to the ability to:
options: Assemble smaller services into larger business processes
Store all data in one file

questions.q: Which of the following best distinguishes web services from a simple script?
options: Web services are designed to expose machine-readable functionality over standard protocols
Scripts always use a service registry
Scripts are always deployed across clouds

questions.q: SOAP is generally associated with:
options: A lightweight REST-based protocol with format-free payloads
An XML-based messaging protocol with a defined contract and standards

questions.q: REST is best characterized as:
options: A protocol that requires a fixed WSDL standard only
An architectural style for stateless communication using HTTP methods and resources

questions.q: Compared with SOAP, REST commonly favors:
options: Verbose XML-heavy contracts and strict WS-* standards
Lightweight resource-based communication with JSON or XML over HTTP
Only binary protocols for all service interactions

questions.q: The publish-subscribe model is most useful when:
options: A sender needs to send a message to every interested receiver without direct point-to-point coupling
A database is used in local memory only
A hypervisor must isolate guest OS instances
Two systems need to physically share a disk

questions.q: In a message broker-based system, a topic or channel is used to:
options: Store local files permanently on a desktop
Organize messages for subscribers interested in a related stream of events
Replace the role of a hypervisor

questions.q: Event-driven communication is especially suitable for:
options: Systems where components react to changes or events asynchronously

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a system of systems?
options: A single monolithic application used by one company
Multiple independent systems connected and coordinated to achieve a larger goal
A single VM hosting many containers

questions.q: Virtualization is best defined as:
options: The process of replicating a network cable in software
The abstraction of physical resources into logical virtual resources
The removal of all hardware from a system
A form of manually writing device drivers

questions.q: The primary need for virtualization in cloud computing is to:
options: Improve resource utilization, isolation, and flexible provisioning

questions.q: Which benefit is most directly associated with virtualization?
options: Higher resource consolidation and easier migration

questions.q: A virtual machine is:
options: A software implementation of a computer system that runs an operating system
A physical server without any guest OS

questions.q: A hypervisor is responsible for:
options: Creating and managing virtual machines by abstracting hardware resources
Running business logic in application code only

questions.q: A Type-1 hypervisor is also called a bare-metal hypervisor because it:
options: Runs directly on the physical hardware
Runs inside a host operating system
Needs a cloud gateway to function

questions.q: A Type-2 hypervisor is typically installed:
options: Directly on the metal with no host OS
On top of an existing host operating system

questions.q: Full virtualization differs from para-virtualization because full virtualization:
options: Requires guest OS modification to communicate with the hypervisor
Allows unmodified guest operating systems to run by emulating hardware interfaces

questions.q: Hardware-assisted virtualization is mainly enabled by:
options: Application-specific CPU features that help trap and virtualize privileged instructions

questions.q: Server virtualization is most useful when an organization wants to:
options: Run multiple operating systems on one physical server
Use a single machine for only one workload forever

questions.q: Desktop virtualization primarily aims to:
options: Host user desktops in a virtual environment, often centralized or remote

questions.q: Application virtualization is used to:
options: Run an application in a virtualized environment independent of the host OS installation
Replace the CPU with a software bus
Serialize all storage into a flat file
Deploy one network switch per workload

questions.q: Storage virtualization allows:
options: Physical storage devices to appear as a pooled or abstract logical resource
A VM to replace all CPU cycles
A hypervisor to manage no disks
Only local file systems without network access

questions.q: Network virtualization often includes:
options: Virtual NICs, virtual switches, and logical networks
One permanent public IP per host

questions.q: OS-level virtualization is most closely associated with:
options: Running multiple isolated user spaces on the same kernel
Emulating a complete hardware platform for each VM
Creating a single host-only storage layer

questions.q: Containerization is different from full virtualization because containers usually:
options: Share the host OS kernel while isolating application processes
Require a separate guest OS for each application

questions.q: Which comparison is most accurate about a virtual machine and a container?
options: A VM includes a guest OS and virtualized hardware, while a container usually packages an app and its dependencies on a shared host OS
A container is always heavier than a VM
A VM cannot run multiple processes, while a container can only run one process
They are identical in isolation and lifecycle

questions.q: Instruction-set-level virtualization is primarily concerned with:
options: Virtualizing CPU instruction execution or ISA interfaces

questions.q: Which virtualization layer is directly responsible for managing guest operating systems over hardware?
Library or API-level virtualization is most relevant when:
options: Applications need to interact with a virtualized version of an API or library behavior
A host OS is being replaced entirely

questions.q: A hypervisor-based virtualization architecture typically includes:
options: Physical hardware, a hypervisor, and one or more guest VMs
Only a base OS and a browser

questions.q: VM isolation is important because it prevents:
options: A guest VM from affecting other VMs or the host beyond its permitted resources
All cloud users from sharing storage
Any scheduling decisions from being made
Containers from running on the same host

questions.q: VM migration is primarily used to:
options: Move a running VM between physical hosts for maintenance, load balancing, or fault tolerance
Convert a hypervisor into a database

questions.q: CPU virtualization is mainly concerned with:
options: Allowing multiple VMs to share CPU time through scheduling and privileged instruction handling
Removing the need for an OS

questions.q: Memory overcommitment in virtualization means:
options: Allocating more virtual memory than the physical memory available, relying on paging or demand management
Never mapping memory pages to storage

questions.q: I/O virtualization is necessary because:
options: Guest VMs must share or access storage and devices through emulated or virtualized interfaces
No device drivers are needed in cloud

questions.q: A virtual NIC is best described as:
options: A logical network interface exposed to a VM, connected through a virtual switch or bridge

questions.q: Which tool is commonly associated with desktop virtualization and VM management in enterprise environments?
Which virtualization technology is widely used for Linux-based KVM environments and supports efficient native performance?
Which of the following technologies is most closely associated with container runtime and orchestration in modern cloud platforms?
A disaster recovery plan for virtualized workloads often relies on:
options: Snapshots, replication, and failover to alternate hosts or regions
Replacing every VM with a single bare-metal server

questions.q: RPO and RTO are relevant to virtualization and disaster recovery because they define:
options: The time allowed for data loss and restoration after failure
The number of VMs on a host
The CPU count of a VM

sections.name: Unit III - Cloud Architecture, Services, Storage, and Deployment

questions.q: A layered cloud architecture usually separates concerns such as:
options: Physical resources, virtualization, management, service, and client layers
Only one single backend service layer

questions.q: In a cloud architecture, the front end typically represents:
options: The user-facing interfaces and clients that access cloud services

questions.q: The back end in a cloud architecture most likely includes:
options: Datacenters, storage, servers, networking, and middleware services

questions.q: The NIST definition of cloud computing emphasizes that cloud services are:
options: Delivered over a network and accessed on demand, with pooled resources and measured usage
Only available with manual procurement releases
Equivalent to a single private datacenter

questions.q: Which NIST characteristic is best illustrated by a user starting a VM in a few minutes without contacting a technician?
In IaaS, the cloud provider is primarily responsible for:
options: Installing and managing the application code
Provisioning the underlying hardware, virtualization, and infrastructure services
Defining the business logic of an application

questions.q: In PaaS, the customer typically manages:
options: The physical data center and hypervisors only
The deployed application and application configuration while the provider manages runtime and platform services

questions.q: In SaaS, the customer typically focuses on:
options: The operating system and server maintenance
Using the provided application without managing underlying infrastructure or platform concerns

questions.q: Which of the following is a typical example of IaaS?
Which of the following is a typical example of PaaS?
Which of the following is a typical example of SaaS?
The responsibility model in cloud computing means that:
options: The provider and customer share responsibilities differently depending on the service model
Only the customer is responsible for all infrastructure layers
Only the provider is responsible for all runtime concerns
Responsibility is irrelevant once a service is deployed

questions.q: A public cloud deployment model is best suited when:
options: An organization wants shared infrastructure available to many customers over the internet
Only one company uses a dedicated environment
The organization wants no external connectivity
A single VM must be permanently retired

questions.q: A private cloud is typically characterized by:
options: Exclusive use by one organization, often on-premises or dedicated
Open shared public access to all users
A single public subscription with no isolation

questions.q: A hybrid cloud is most useful when:
options: An organization wants to combine private infrastructure with public cloud resources for flexibility and compliance
No cloud resources are used at all
A single provider must store all data in one region
Only one VM runs a browser app

questions.q: A community cloud would be most appropriate for:
options: A shared infrastructure used by several organizations with common concerns, such as government or research institutions
A single app server with no user access

questions.q: Which of the following is a major architectural design challenge in cloud systems?
options: Guaranteed zero downtime for all workloads
Scalability, availability, reliability, security, and performance management
No need for replication or backups

questions.q: Vendor lock-in is a concern because it may:
options: Make it difficult and costly to migrate workloads or data to another cloud provider

questions.q: An SLA in cloud computing is best described as:
options: A service-level contract that defines expected performance, availability, and responsibilities

questions.q: Cloud storage is best described as:
options: Storage that is provided and managed over a network as a service

questions.q: Object storage is best suited for:
options: Large-scale unstructured data such as images, logs, and backups

questions.q: Block storage is typically used for:
options: High-performance volumes attached to virtual machines like databases and operating systems

questions.q: File storage is most commonly used when:
options: Multiple users need shared access to files through a hierarchical directory structure
A workload only needs a single in-memory variable
A VM does not need storage

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares object storage and block storage?
options: Object storage stores data as immutable objects with metadata and keys, while block storage offers raw volumes attached to VMs
Object storage is always faster than block storage for databases
Block storage uses keys and metadata, while object storage uses raw bytes only
They are the same concept under different names

questions.q: Durability in cloud storage refers to:
options: The likelihood that data will remain intact and retrievable over time
The number of network ports available
The speed of a single CPU core
The price of a virtualization license

questions.q: Availability in cloud storage is primarily about:
options: Whether data and services are accessible when needed
Only the physical location of a data center
The color scheme of the dashboard

questions.q: Which cloud storage feature is most directly related to creating alternate copies of data for resilience?
Storage-as-a-Service is useful when an organization wants to:
options: Consume storage capacity as an on-demand managed service without owning the infrastructure

questions.q: Amazon S3 is primarily a:
In Amazon S3, a bucket is best described as:
options: A container for storing objects under a unique namespace

questions.q: Which S3 feature is used to protect against accidental deletion or overwrite by retaining multiple versions of an object?
Lifecycle policies in S3 are primarily used to:
options: Automatically move objects between storage classes based on age and access patterns

questions.q: Which S3 storage class is designed for data that is infrequently accessed but still requires rapid retrieval?
Amazon EBS is best classified as:
options: Block storage attached to EC2 instances

questions.q: Azure Blob Storage is primarily intended for:
options: Unstructured object data such as files and media
An OS kernel image with no metadata

questions.q: Azure Disk Storage is best compared to:
options: Amazon EBS block storage attached to virtual machines

questions.q: A cloud storage design that chooses object storage over block storage is most likely optimizing for:
options: Scalability and distributed access to unstructured data

sections.name: Unit IV - Resource Management and Cloud Security

questions.q: Inter-cloud computing most directly refers to:
options: A single provider environment with no external federation
Collaboration and resource sharing among multiple cloud providers or clouds
Only local file sharing across machines
A private network that never connects to the internet

questions.q: Cloud federation is best described as:
options: The aggregation of different cloud environments under shared policies and resource management
A direct physical cable between two desktops
A single VM cluster without networking

questions.q: Cloud bursting is most useful when:
options: A private cloud needs to use public cloud resources during peak load
Only one user accesses a VM

questions.q: Resource discovery in a distributed cloud environment is used to:
options: Find available resources, services, and providers to meet workload requirements

questions.q: Static provisioning differs from dynamic provisioning because static provisioning:
options: Allocates resources in advance based on prediction rather than real-time demand

questions.q: Dynamic provisioning is most useful when:
options: A system must scale resources in response to actual workload changes in real time
The provider does not monitor usage

questions.q: Vertical scaling means:
options: Increasing the capacity of an existing instance, such as more CPU or memory
Creating a completely new cloud account
Adding more network security groups only

questions.q: Horizontal scaling means:
options: Adding more instances to distribute load

questions.q: Demand-based provisioning mainly responds to:
options: Actual current demand or usage patterns

questions.q: Reservation-based provisioning is appropriate when:
options: A customer wants guaranteed capacity for predictable workloads by reserving resources ahead of time
There is no need for performance guarantees

questions.q: Threshold-based provisioning often triggers when:
options: Resource utilization crosses a pre-defined threshold such as CPU or memory usage

questions.q: Predictive provisioning is based on:
options: Forecasting future demand using historical patterns and trends

questions.q: The CIA triad in cloud security refers to:
Confidentiality in cloud security aims to protect data from:
Integrity in cloud security ensures that data is:
options: Accessible only to a single user
Protected from unauthorized alteration and remains trustworthy
Stored in immutable object storage only

questions.q: Authentication is the process of:
options: Verifying the identity of a user or system

questions.q: Authorization is the process of:
options: Checking whether an authenticated principal is allowed to perform an action

questions.q: Least privilege in IAM means that a user or service should:
options: Receive the narrowest set of permissions necessary to do its job
Receive no permissions and no roles

questions.q: Multi-factor authentication is used to:
options: Require more than one factor for identity verification, such as password plus OTP or hardware token

questions.q: Role-based access control is useful because it:
options: Assigns permissions according to job roles rather than individual user settings alone
Requires every user to have an administrator account

questions.q: A common cloud security challenge is a data breach because it may:
options: Expose sensitive information through weak controls, misconfiguration, or compromised credentials

questions.q: A shared technology vulnerability is primarily a risk because:
options: Multiple tenants may rely on the same underlying infrastructure components, and a flaw in one layer can affect others
Only one tenant exists in a public cloud
It is only relevant to on-premises storage

questions.q: SaaS security typically focuses on:
options: Tenant isolation, application security, access control, and secure configuration of the SaaS platform
Operating system installation from source code

questions.q: VM escape is a security concern because it allows:
options: A guest VM to break out of the isolation boundary and interact with the host or other VMs
A VM to move between clouds without authentication
A guest OS to replace a CPU
A data center to ignore backups

questions.q: Hypervisor security is important because the hypervisor:
options: Controls access to physical resources and can be a critical attack surface if compromised
Is only used for application code
Is never involved in network communication

questions.q: Which security standard is focused broadly on information security management systems?
ISO 27017 and ISO 27018 are relevant to cloud security primarily because they:
options: Provide guidance for cloud-specific security and privacy controls

questions.q: SOC 2 reports are important to cloud customers because they help assess:
options: A provider's controls related to security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy
Only the physical power usage of a data center
The efficiency of one storage bucket only
The price of on-demand CPU instances

questions.q: The purpose of a security governance framework is to ensure that:
options: Policies, controls, risks, and compliance obligations are defined and enforced consistently

questions.q: Identity federation in cloud access is designed to:
options: Allow users to use credentials across trusted domains or providers

questions.q: A temporary credential in IAM is typically used for:
options: Short-lived access to resources under limited time windows
Permanent root access to every account

questions.q: Data loss prevention in cloud systems is usually supported by a combination of:
options: Encryption, backup, access control, and monitoring practices

questions.q: In the context of cloud security, a denial-of-service attack seeks to:
options: Make services unavailable or heavily degraded by overwhelming resources

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the shared responsibility model?
options: The provider and customer share security and operational responsibilities according to the service model
The provider owns every responsibility and the customer has none
The customer owns all physical hardware, while the provider owns no services
Responsibility is always 50 percent split regardless of service type

questions.q: Cloud governance is most concerned with:
options: Policies, compliance, cost, access, and accountability for cloud resources
Only a single VM's CPU temperature

questions.q: Which of the following is a strong cloud security control for protecting data at rest?
A zero-trust security model assumes that:
options: No user, device, or network segment is inherently trusted; verification is required continuously
All internal traffic is always safe and needs no validation
Only a private network requires access control
Authentication ends after one login forever

sections.name: Unit V - Hadoop, VirtualBox, Federation, and Advanced Cloud Technologies

questions.q: Hadoop is mainly designed for:
options: Distributed storage and processing of large-scale data sets
Local file system optimization at the byte level

questions.q: The Hadoop Distributed File System is best known for:
options: Storing large files across multiple machines with fault tolerance and replication
Keeping all data in a single disk

questions.q: In HDFS, the NameNode is responsible for:
options: Tracking file metadata and the namespace of the cluster
Uploading object data to a cloud bucket
Executing application code in the browser

questions.q: DataNodes in HDFS primarily:
options: Store actual blocks of data and serve read and write requests
Store only metadata for a registry

questions.q: The fault tolerance in HDFS is achieved largely through:
options: Replication of data blocks across multiple machines

questions.q: MapReduce is designed for:
options: Parallel processing of large data sets using map and reduce phases
Operating a single application on a laptop

questions.q: In the MapReduce model, the map phase is primarily responsible for:
options: Reading input data and transforming it into intermediate key-value pairs

questions.q: The reduce phase in MapReduce typically:
options: Aggregates and summarizes intermediate key-value outputs produced by the map phase
Transforms a VM into a browser

questions.q: Data locality in Hadoop is important because it allows:
options: Computation to occur close to the data, reducing network transfer and improving efficiency
All data to be stored in a single memory heap
Only a single DataNode to serve all requests

questions.q: VirtualBox is best described as:
options: A desktop virtualization product used to run guest operating systems on a host machine

questions.q: Guest Additions in VirtualBox are intended to:
options: Improve integration between the guest OS and the host, such as shared folders and display support

questions.q: Snapshots in virtual machine management are used to:
options: Capture the state of a VM at a point in time for recovery or rollback
Remove all disks from a host

questions.q: Which network mode in VirtualBox attaches a VM to a network similar to a physical network and allows it to appear as a separate machine on the LAN?
Google App Engine is best classified as:
options: A Platform-as-a-Service offering for deploying web applications and services on managed infrastructure

questions.q: OpenStack is primarily known as:
options: An open-source cloud platform that provides compute, storage, networking, and identity services

questions.q: The major OpenStack service responsible for compute resources is:
Neutron in OpenStack is mainly associated with:
Swift in OpenStack is primarily used for:
Cloud federation is valuable because it enables:
options: Interoperability, resource sharing, and portability across multiple cloud providers
The permanent binding of all workloads to one data center

questions.q: A federated cloud service is most likely to support:
options: Cross-cloud application composition and shared resource discovery across providers
A single local file system only

questions.q: Which of the following is a likely future direction of federated cloud ecosystems?
options: Multi-cloud interoperability, hybrid cloud portability, and edge-cloud integration
Disabling all networking for cloud resources

questions.q: A cloud environment that uses containers, microservices, dynamic orchestration, and API-driven integration is best described as:
Docker is primarily used to:
options: Package applications and dependencies into portable containers
Replace the need for a hypervisor

questions.q: Kubernetes is best described as:
options: A container orchestration platform for managing deployment, scaling, and networking of containers
A network protocol for DNS only

questions.q: A microservice architecture emphasizes:
options: Small, independently deployable services that work together to form a larger application
A single monolithic program with no service boundaries

questions.q: Function-as-a-Service is especially suitable for:
options: Event-triggered, short-lived workloads that scale automatically with demand

questions.q: AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, and Google Cloud Functions are examples of:
CI/CD in cloud engineering mainly improves:
options: Continuous integration and continuous delivery or deployment for faster and safer software changes

questions.q: Infrastructure as Code is primarily used to:
options: Define and manage cloud resources through code, enabling repeatable provisioning and automation

questions.q: Terraform is widely used for:
options: Declarative infrastructure provisioning across cloud providers and environments

questions.q: Observability in cloud systems focuses on understanding system behavior through:
A load balancer in cloud computing is used to:
options: Distribute incoming traffic across multiple application instances to improve performance and availability
Store raw data in object buckets

questions.q: A content delivery network is mainly designed to:
options: Cache and deliver content closer to users, reducing latency and improving load times
Replace the hypervisor on a host

questions.q: Autoscaling in cloud environments helps by:
options: Adjusting resource capacity automatically according to demand and policies
Creating a static VM pool with no change

questions.q: Which of the following is a key benefit of edge computing for IoT systems?
options: Lower latency and reduced bandwidth use by processing data closer to the source
Higher cost by forcing all data to a central cloud
No security concerns at the device level
No need for sensors or gateways

questions.q: A cloud database is best characterized by:
options: A database service managed over the network, often with scalability and provisioning features built in
Only a flat file on a local workstation
A raw storage volume without indexing

questions.q: Which of the following is the best description of NoSQL databases?
options: Databases designed for flexible schemas and large-scale distributed workloads, often without full relational constraints
Only spreadsheets managed by cloud vendors
A hypervisor feature for VM snapshots

questions.q: CAP theorem addresses trade-offs in distributed systems between:
options: Fault tolerance, load balancing, and metadata

questions.q: Event-driven architecture is most closely associated with:
options: Reactive workflows where services respond to events and messages asynchronously
A database with no event emitter

questions.q: An API gateway is typically used to:
options: Centralize routing, authentication, rate limiting, and composition for multiple microservices
Replace the need for a hypervisor
Provide random access memory to a VM

questions.q: Service discovery in a microservice environment helps by:
options: Allowing services to find and communicate with one another dynamically
Mapping each service to a single static IP forever

questions.q: A message queue is mainly used to:
options: Decouple producers and consumers by buffering and delivering events asynchronously
Replace the need for a database
Connect a browser directly to a DNS server

questions.q: A Virtual Private Cloud is designed to:
options: Provide a logically isolated private cloud section within a public cloud provider network
Lock a customer to a single region always

questions.q: A security group is most similar to:
options: A firewall rule set controlling allowed ingress and egress traffic

questions.q: A VPN in cloud architectures is typically used to:
options: Create a secure private connection between networks over a public network
Reduce all traffic to a single route
Store object data in a bucket

questions.q: Disaster recovery planning in the cloud often emphasizes:
options: Backup, replication, failover, RPO, and RTO targets
Permanent reliance on a single availability zone

questions.q: RTO is best defined as:
options: The maximum acceptable time to restore a service after a disruption
The amount of data lost since the last backup
The number of replicas created in a region
The lifetime of an IAM token

questions.q: RPO is best defined as:
options: The maximum acceptable age of data that may be lost during recovery
The time a VM takes to boot
The maximum CPU load before autoscaling
The size of a DNS record

questions.q: A multi-region cloud architecture is typically adopted to:
options: Improve resilience, disaster recovery, and global availability

questions.q: FinOps in cloud management focuses on:
options: Managing cloud cost, usage, and accountability as a financial and operational discipline
The design of local private networks only

questions.q: Reserved instances or reserved capacity are typically chosen to:
options: Reduce long-term costs for predictable workloads with stable demand

questions.q: Spot or preemptible instances are best suited for:
options: Fault-tolerant, flexible workloads that can handle interruptions

questions.q: Confidential computing is intended to protect:
options: Data while it is in use within secure hardware-enforced trusted execution environments
Only static files at rest without encryption

questions.q: A common goal of cloud migration strategies such as lift-and-shift, replatforming, and refactoring is to:
options: Move existing workloads to the cloud while balancing speed, cost, and architecture improvement
Eliminate all applications from a company

questions.q: Vendor lock-in is a concern primarily because it may:
options: Increase migration difficulty, cost, and dependence on one provider's proprietary services
Improve public internet speed for all users
Reduce the need for IAM and monitoring

questions.q: A cloud SLA is important because it defines:
options: Expected service availability, support commitments, and responsibilities between provider and customer
Only the DNS record of one service
The host operating system version only
The amount of memory in a single laptop
